skill.name: pinchbench
skill.description: Run PinchBench benchmarks to evaluate OpenClaw agent performance across real-world tasks, compare model behavior, and prepare leaderboard-ready benchmark results.
skill.summary: Evaluate OpenClaw agent models with repeatable PinchBench benchmark tasks.
skill.author: pinchbench

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms remote pipe-to-shell install, Python exec grading, OpenClaw CLI execution, workspace mutation, credential handling, and default upload behavior. Many markdown, fixture, ANSI color, and normal import hits are false positives. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh during Docker builds.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version, verify checksums, or vendor a reviewed installer before executing it.

remediation.issue: Task markdown grading code is executed with Python exec in the main process.
remediation.suggestion: Run grading code in a locked-down sandbox or replace embedded code with a constrained grading API.

remediation.issue: Benchmark execution creates, deletes, and runs OpenClaw agents through local CLI commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit confirmation step and recommend a dedicated benchmark workspace and throwaway agent profile.

remediation.issue: Leaderboard upload can send benchmark results and host metadata to the PinchBench service.
remediation.suggestion: Default to local-only runs or show a clear pre-upload disclosure with all submitted metadata fields.

remediation.issue: Installed user skills are copied into benchmark workspaces.
remediation.suggestion: Make skill copying opt-in and allow users to select specific public skills for benchmark tasks.

remediation.issue: Provider and leaderboard tokens are read from environment variables and local config.
remediation.suggestion: Document token scopes, avoid logging secrets, and support offline validation paths where possible.

semantic_findings.title: Default Leaderboard Upload Sends System Metadata
semantic_findings.description: The benchmark uploads results unless --no-upload is used, and the payload includes OS, Python, CPU, memory, and hostname-derived metadata. This is useful for leaderboard context but should be explicit because it leaves the local machine.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The upload path is called by default when upload is not disabled, and lib_upload builds metadata from platform and /proc values. The behavior is direct and documented in code.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code iterates user skill directories and uses shutil.copytree into the benchmark workspace. Exposure depends on local skill contents, so severity is medium rather than critical.

content.value_statement: Model teams need repeatable evidence for agent performance. PinchBench runs structured OpenClaw tasks and produces comparable scores for analysis and leaderboard submission.
actual_capabilities: Runs 23 OpenClaw benchmark tasks from the included tasks directory.
Selects all tasks, automated-only tasks, or specific task IDs.
Creates or recreates OpenClaw agents for a selected model and workspace.
Grades tasks with automated checks, LLM judge scoring, or hybrid scoring.
Saves result files with scores, timing, usage, and efficiency metrics.
Registers and uploads leaderboard submissions when a token is configured.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10, uv, and an installed OpenClaw CLI.
Benchmark runs can execute OpenClaw agents and modify temporary workspaces.
Some workflows require network access, model credentials, or upload tokens.
Included binary assets should be trusted before running the full benchmark.

use_cases.title: Compare model performance
use_cases.description: Run the same OpenClaw task suite across multiple models and compare scores, cost, and completion time.

use_cases.title: Regression test OpenClaw workflows
use_cases.description: Check whether recent agent, skill, or environment changes affect task completion quality.

use_cases.title: Design new benchmark tasks
use_cases.description: Use the task template and grading patterns to add repeatable evaluations for new agent workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Run a quick benchmark
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation with the automated subset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run PinchBench with MODEL on the automated-only suite and save the results locally without uploading.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two models
prompt_templates.prompt: Run PinchBench for MODEL_A and MODEL_B on the same task suite, then summarize score, cost, and timing differences.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate weak tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced quality analysis after a benchmark run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the latest PinchBench results and identify tasks below 0.5 score with likely causes and next debugging steps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a custom suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a focused PinchBench suite for workflow automation tasks, include grading criteria, and explain how to run it safely.

output_examples.input: Run the automated-only suite for one model without uploading.
output_examples.output: The run finishes with per-task scores, a total score, token usage, cost metrics, and a local result file path.
The comparison highlights score differences, failed tasks, execution time changes, and cost efficiency tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Design a new benchmark task for email triage.
output_examples.output: The task draft includes a prompt, expected behavior, grading criteria, and automated checks for repeatable scoring.

best_practices: Run with upload disabled until you understand what data will be submitted.
Use a dedicated benchmark workspace and test credentials for model providers.
Review custom task grading code before allowing it to run locally.
anti_patterns: Do not run the full suite on a primary workspace before a sanity check.
Do not upload benchmark results before reviewing metadata and token settings.
Do not add custom tasks with broad filesystem or shell access in grading code.

faq.question: What does PinchBench evaluate?
faq.answer: It evaluates OpenClaw agent performance across practical tasks such as files, email, research, coding, and workflows.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code marketplace surfaces.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes for model validation, provider calls, registration, and leaderboard uploads. Local runs can skip upload.

faq.question: Where are results stored?
faq.answer: Benchmark results are written to the configured results directory as local result files.

faq.question: Can I run only selected tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. The runner supports all tasks, automated-only tasks, or a comma-separated list of task IDs.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing?
faq.answer: Review command execution, grading code execution, data upload behavior, copied skills, and bundled binary assets.
